citation: World Health Organization. WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. 2020.
key_use_and_limit: Adults should limit sedentary time and replace it with physical activity of any intensity; the guideline does not prescribe a universal break interval.

citation: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Adult Activity: An Overview.
key_use_and_limit: Move more and sit less; some activity is better than none. Break reminders do not replace weekly aerobic and strengthening recommendations.

evidence_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of acute randomized crossover studies
citation: Gale JT, Martin H, Haszard JJ, Peddie MC. The Acute Effects of Interrupting Prolonged Sitting With Regular Activity Breaks on Postprandial Glucose and Insulin in Adults. Obesity Reviews. 2026. doi:10.1111/obr.70152. PMID:42070794.
key_use_and_limit: Activity breaks produced small-to-moderate acute reductions in post-meal glucose and insulin; walking breaks generally performed best. These are acute laboratory outcomes, not proof of long-term disease prevention.

citation: Duran AT, et al. Breaking Up Prolonged Sitting to Improve Cardiometabolic Risk: Dose-Response Analysis of a Randomized Crossover Trial. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2023;55(5):847-855. doi:10.1249/MSS.0000000000003109. PMID:36728338.
key_use_and_limit: In 11 middle- and older-age adults, five minutes of light walking every 30 minutes was the only tested dose that significantly attenuated the glucose outcome; all tested doses affected systolic blood pressure. Acute, very small study.

citation: Loh R, et al. Effects of Interrupting Prolonged Sitting with Physical Activity Breaks on Blood Glucose, Insulin and Triacylglycerol Measures: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Sports Med. 2020. PMID:31552570.
key_use_and_limit: Breaking prolonged sitting with activity can attenuate acute postprandial metabolic responses; effects vary by population and protocol.

citation: Diaz KM, et al. Evaluating movement breaks as a public health strategy to mitigate the harms of prolonged sitting: a large-scale pragmatic intervention. Br J Sports Med. 2026;60:1208-1217. doi:10.1136/bjsports-2025-111221.
key_use_and_limit: Five-minute walking breaks every 30, 60, or 120 minutes were tested for two weeks in real life. Every 30 minutes showed stronger self-reported psychosocial change; hourly breaks offered the best feasibility/effectiveness balance. Self-selected arms, self-reported outcomes, brief follow-up.

citation: Cochrane. Different types of work-break schedules for preventing musculoskeletal symptoms and disorders in healthy workers. Updated 2025. doi:10.1002/14651858.CD012886.pub3.
key_use_and_limit: Available trials were small and very uncertain; no optimal break frequency or type can be declared.

citation: Albulescu P, et al. Give me a break! A systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy of micro-breaks for increasing well-being and performance. PLoS One. 2022;17:e0272460. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0272460.
key_use_and_limit: Microbreaks showed small benefits for vigor and fatigue; the pooled performance effect was not significant overall and depended on task and break features.

citation: Radwan A, et al. The effectiveness of active microbreaks in improving occupational health and work performance: a systematic review. Cogent Engineering. 2022. doi:10.1080/23311916.2022.2026206.
key_use_and_limit: Potential benefits were reported, but the controlled evidence base was small and heterogeneous.

citation: Leppe-Zamora M, et al. Prompt-based interventions to reduce sedentary behaviour: systematic review and meta-analysis. 2025. PMID:40514667.
key_use_and_limit: Digital prompts can reduce sitting, but evidence for durability and downstream health outcomes remains limited.

citation: Shrestha N, et al. Workplace interventions for reducing sitting at work. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2018. PMID:29926475.
key_use_and_limit: Sit-stand desks reduce workplace sitting in the short and medium term, but long-term and health-outcome evidence was low quality or uncertain.

citation: Sheppard AL, Wolffsohn JS. Digital eye strain: prevalence, measurement and amelioration. BMJ Open Ophthalmol. 2018;3:e000146. doi:10.1136/bmjophth-2018-000146. PMID:29963645.
key_use_and_limit: Digital eye strain is multifactorial; viewing behaviour, dry-eye mechanisms, refractive correction, environment and ergonomics all matter.

citation: Kaur K, et al. Digital Eye Strain—A Comprehensive Review. Ophthalmol Ther. 2022. PMCID:PMC9434525.
key_use_and_limit: Supports a multi-factor model and cautious use of break, viewing, blink and workstation advice.

citation: Talens-Estarelles C, et al. The effects of breaks on digital eye strain, dry eye and binocular vision: Testing the 20-20-20 rule. Cont Lens Anterior Eye. 2023;46:101744. doi:10.1016/j.clae.2022.101744. PMID:35963776.
key_use_and_limit: Reminder-supported 20-20-20 behaviour improved symptoms while reminders were used in a small symptomatic sample, but objective dry-eye signs did not change and effects were not maintained after reminders stopped.

citation: Al-Mohtaseb Z, et al. The Relationship Between Dry Eye Disease and Digital Screen Use. Clin Ophthalmol. 2021. PMID:34531649.
key_use_and_limit: Reduced or incomplete blinking and ocular-surface exposure are plausible contributors to screen-related dry-eye symptoms.

citation: Pucker AD, et al. Digital Screen Use and Dry Eye: Updated Perspectives. 2024. PMCID:PMC11416787.
key_use_and_limit: The screen–dry-eye relationship is real but heterogeneous; product advice should avoid implying one universal mechanism or cure.

citation: Ashwini DL, et al. Evaluation of a blink-reminder software in digital device users. 2021. PMCID:PMC8597488.
key_use_and_limit: Software cues may increase blink behaviour and improve subjective symptoms, but the evidence is limited and does not validate constant high-frequency nudging.

citation: Downie LE, et al. Blue-light filtering spectacle lenses for visual performance, sleep, and macular health in adults. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2023. PMID:37593770.
key_use_and_limit: Blue-light filtering lenses probably provide little or no short-term benefit for eye strain; evidence for sleep and retinal outcomes is uncertain.

citation: Mataftsi A, et al. Digital eye strain interventions: systematic review. 2023. PMID:36977430.
key_use_and_limit: Blue filters were not clearly effective; ergonomic and exposure-management measures are more defensible, though evidence quality varies.

citation: American Academy of Ophthalmology. Computers, Digital Devices, and Eye Strain.
key_use_and_limit: Practical comfort guidance: breaks, appropriate viewing, glare and brightness management, and evaluation of persistent symptoms.

citation: American Academy of Ophthalmology. Digital Devices and Your Eyes.
key_use_and_limit: Current consumer digital-device blue light has not been shown to cause eye disease; discomfort should not be marketed as retinal damage.

citation: American Academy of Ophthalmology. Should You Be Worried About Blue Light?
key_use_and_limit: Do not use blue-light fear as the product health rationale.

citation: Hoe VCW, et al. Ergonomic interventions for preventing work-related musculoskeletal disorders of the upper limb and neck among office workers. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2018. PMID:30350850.
key_use_and_limit: Evidence for many office ergonomic interventions is low or unclear; arm support or alternative mouse and supplementary breaks may help in some contexts, but broad prevention claims are not justified.

citation: Slater D, et al. Sit Up Straight: Time to Re-evaluate. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther. 2019. PMID:31366294.
key_use_and_limit: No single ideal posture has been established as a universal pain-prevention target; comfort, task fit and variation are better product concepts.

citation: Louw S, et al. Effectiveness of exercise in office workers with neck pain: A systematic review and meta-analysis. S Afr J Physiother. 2017. PMID:30135909.
key_use_and_limit: Strengthening may reduce pain in symptomatic office workers, but this does not make generic exercise reminders preventive treatment.

citation: Chen X, et al. Workplace-Based Interventions for Neck Pain in Office Workers: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Phys Ther. 2018;98(1):40-62. PMID:29088401.
key_use_and_limit: Neck and shoulder-specific strengthening helped symptomatic workers in some trials but did not show general-population prevention; evidence for work breaks was inconsistent.

citation: Jones LB, et al. The influence of exercise on pain, disability and quality of life in office workers with chronic neck pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Appl Ergon. 2024. PMID:38219373.
key_use_and_limit: Recent evidence remains heterogeneous and certainty is limited; avoid treatment claims in a general wellness app.

citation: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration. Computer Workstations eTool.
key_use_and_limit: There is no one correct workstation or posture for everyone; provides practical adjustable setup goals.

citation: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration. Computer Workstations: Good Working Positions.
key_use_and_limit: Change position, make small adjustments and periodically stand or walk; static perfection is not the goal.

citation: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration. Computer Workstations: Monitors.
key_use_and_limit: Monitor placement should reduce awkward neck positions and glare; guidance is a starting point, not a personalized prescription.

citation: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration. Computer Workstations: Keyboards.
key_use_and_limit: Keep input devices close enough for relaxed shoulders and elbows and relatively neutral wrists.

citation: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration. Computer Workstations: Pointer/Mouse.
key_use_and_limit: Reduce reaching and support a comfortable, relatively neutral wrist and forearm position.

citation: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety. Working in a Standing Position / Sit-Stand Workstations.
key_use_and_limit: Recommendations vary; gradual adaptation and position alternation matter more than a rigid ratio.

citation: MacEwen BT, MacDonald DJ, Burr JF. A systematic review of standing and treadmill desks in the workplace. Prev Med. 2015. PMID:25448843.
key_use_and_limit: Evidence for health and well-being outcomes was mixed; productivity effects were generally small but research quality varied.

citation: Podrekar N, et al. The effects of cycle and treadmill desks on work performance and cognitive function: a meta-analysis. Work. 2020. PMID:32116273.
key_use_and_limit: Active workstations can affect work performance, often through motor and typing demands rather than broad cognitive impairment.

citation: Medina-Inojosa JR, et al. Effect of Active Workstations on Neurocognitive Performance and Typing Capabilities: A Randomized Clinical Trial. 2024. PMCID:PMC11262529.
key_use_and_limit: Active workstations may be feasible for some tasks, but device type and task demands matter.

citation: Larson MJ, et al. Cognitive and typing outcomes measured simultaneously with slow treadmill walking or sitting. PLoS One. 2015. PMID:25874910.
key_use_and_limit: Slow walking produced modest decrements in typing and some cognitive measures in this study; the app should not recommend treadmill use for every task.

citation: Treadmill-desk workplace interventions: systematic review and meta-analysis. BMC Public Health. 2021. doi:10.1186/s12889-021-12094-9.
key_use_and_limit: Treadmill desks increase energy expenditure and reduce sitting, but evidence for durable physiological outcomes is not established.

citation: Fincham GW, et al. Effect of breathwork on stress and mental health: A meta-analysis of randomised-controlled trials. Sci Rep. 2023. PMID:36624160.
key_use_and_limit: Breathwork showed modest self-reported benefits, with heterogeneity and bias concerns. Use as an optional calming exercise, not treatment.

citation: Slow breathing and psychophysiological outcomes: review of mechanisms and evidence. 2023. PMCID:PMC10741869.
key_use_and_limit: Supports gentle paced breathing as optional; avoid forceful hyperventilation or long breath holds.

citation: National Sleep Foundation. The impact of screen use on sleep health across the lifespan: 2024 consensus statement. PMID:38806392.
key_use_and_limit: For adults, evidence is nuanced and consensus is weaker than for children and adolescents; avoid a universal screen curfew presented as clinical fact.

citation: Zhong C, et al. Electronic Screen Use and Sleep Duration and Timing in Adults. JAMA Netw Open. 2025. PMID:40146105.
key_use_and_limit: Pre-bed screen use was associated with shorter or worse self-reported sleep; cross-sectional design does not establish causality.

citation: Consensus recommendations for screen use and sleep health. 2025. PMID:40701900.
key_use_and_limit: An optional wind-down tool can focus on bedtime displacement, stimulation and comfort rather than promising that a filter fixes sleep.

evidence_type: Patient guidance from a specialist nonprofit
citation: American Migraine Foundation. Photophobia, light sensitivity and screens.
key_use_and_limit: Bright or flickering light can exacerbate symptoms for some people; provide a dim, static, reduced-motion break mode.

citation: W3C. Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2.
key_use_and_limit: Avoid flashing, provide pause and stop controls, respect reduced motion, and support perceivable and operable alternatives.

citation: Apple Developer. Accessibility and Reduce Motion guidance.
key_use_and_limit: Honor system accessibility settings and build keyboard, VoiceOver, contrast, text-size and reduced-motion support from the start.

citation: National Academies. Dietary Reference Intakes for Water, Potassium, Sodium, Chloride, and Sulfate.
key_use_and_limit: Water needs vary and healthy adults usually regulate intake through thirst and food and fluid sources; arbitrary desktop quotas are not research-backed personalization.

citation: Mayo Clinic. Hyponatremia—Symptoms and causes.
key_use_and_limit: Excessive water intake can be harmful; hydration reminders should be user-defined and off by default.

citation: World Health Organization and International Telecommunication Union. Global standard for safe listening devices and systems.
key_use_and_limit: Safe-listening features require exposure information; a desktop app should not infer acoustic dose from an arbitrary volume percentage.

citation: American Heart Association. Warning Signs of a Heart Attack.
key_use_and_limit: Movement content must instruct users to stop and seek urgent help for chest discomfort, severe unusual shortness of breath, fainting or similar acute symptoms.

citation: NHS and NICE. Cauda equina syndrome and emergency back-pain red flags.
key_use_and_limit: New bladder or bowel dysfunction, saddle numbness or acute leg weakness warrants urgent assessment; the app must not normalize these as ordinary desk discomfort.

citation: American Academy of Ophthalmology. What Are Floaters and Flashes?
key_use_and_limit: Sudden new or increased floaters or flashes can indicate retinal tear or detachment and require prompt eye assessment.

citation: NHS. Detached retina (retinal detachment).
key_use_and_limit: A dark curtain or shadow, sudden blur, flashes or a sudden increase in floaters requires urgent eye care.

citation: US Food and Drug Administration. General Wellness: Policy for Low Risk Devices. Final guidance, January 6, 2026.
key_use_and_limit: Healthy-lifestyle functions unrelated to diagnosis, cure, mitigation, prevention or treatment of disease can remain in general-wellness territory when low risk; intended use and claims matter.

citation: Health Canada. Guidance Document: Software as a Medical Device (SaMD): Definition and Classification.
key_use_and_limit: Software is SaMD when intended for a medical purpose and performing that purpose independently of hardware; intended use and labelling are central.

citation: European Commission MDCG 2019-11 rev.1. Guidance on Qualification and Classification of Software under MDR/IVDR. June 2025.
key_use_and_limit: Qualification and classification depend on intended purpose and the nature of information or action provided.

citation: UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency. Medical devices: software applications.
key_use_and_limit: Explains when an app is a medical device; claims and intended purpose must be controlled.

citation: UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency. Borderlines with medical devices and other products in Great Britain. Updated June 29, 2026.
key_use_and_limit: Wellness and medical boundaries are claim- and function-sensitive; obtain legal and regulatory review before expanding intended purpose.

citation: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada. Guidelines for obtaining meaningful consent.
key_use_and_limit: Consent must be understandable and tied to meaningful choices; optional health and context integrations need separate purpose explanations.

citation: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada. PIPEDA fair information principles.
key_use_and_limit: Limit collection, use, disclosure and retention; protect data with appropriate safeguards.

citation: UK Information Commissioner’s Office. Special category data.
key_use_and_limit: Health data is specially protected; symptom logs and inferred health status require heightened justification and controls.

citation: European Data Protection Board. Guidelines on data protection by design and by default.
key_use_and_limit: Build minimization, local processing, purpose limitation and privacy-protective defaults into architecture rather than adding them later.

citation: California Privacy Protection Agency. CCPA regulations and sensitive personal information.
key_use_and_limit: Health and biometric information can be sensitive personal information; avoid collecting it unless necessary and explicitly controlled.

citation: Apple Developer. MenuBarExtra.
key_use_and_limit: Native entry point for a menu-bar-first macOS app.

citation: Apple Developer. CGEventSource.secondsSinceLastEventType.
key_use_and_limit: Can estimate elapsed time since input events without logging keystrokes; this is an activity proxy, not proof of gaze, sitting or movement.

citation: Apple Developer. HealthKit.
key_use_and_limit: HealthKit is centered on iPhone and Apple Watch and requires user permission; any Mac integration should use a companion app.

citation: Apple Developer. HKHealthStore.isHealthDataAvailable().
key_use_and_limit: On macOS the framework may be present but apps cannot read or write HealthKit data; do not architect direct Mac HealthKit access.

citation: Apple Developer. Defining your app’s Focus filter.
key_use_and_limit: Focus Filters are user-configured app behaviour, not a general public API for silently reading all Focus state.

citation: Apple Developer. App Sandbox.
key_use_and_limit: Mac App Store distribution requires sandboxing; permissions and data access must be minimized.

citation: Apple Developer. EventKit.
key_use_and_limit: Calendar access requires permission. Convert events to ephemeral busy or free intervals and discard titles, attendees and notes.

citation: Apple Developer. SMAppService.
key_use_and_limit: Use supported launch-at-login APIs rather than legacy or private mechanisms.

citation: Apple Developer. User Notifications and notification Human Interface Guidelines.
key_use_and_limit: Wellness nudges should not misuse Time Sensitive or Critical interruption levels and should respect user control.

citation: LookAway. Smart Break Reminder App for Mac.
key_use_and_limit: Strong product patterns include heads-up notices, snooze, idle awareness, app and context suppression, planned breaks, Focus integration and native Mac design.

citation: Dejal. Time Out—Break Reminders.
key_use_and_limit: Mature flexible model with micro and normal breaks, natural-break handling and user customization.

citation: Hovancik J. Stretchly—The break time reminder app.
key_use_and_limit: Cross-platform open-source patterns include idle awareness, do-not-disturb suppression, postpone or skip, and configurable schedules.

citation: BreakTimer. Break reminder app.
key_use_and_limit: Simple customizable schedules, working hours, heads-up notifications and custom messages.

citation: Swartz AM, et al. Prompts to Disrupt Sitting Time and Increase Physical Activity at Work. Prev Chronic Dis. 2014.
key_use_and_limit: Prompts can alter workday sitting patterns, but a desktop proxy must not claim to directly measure sitting.

citation: American Academy of Ophthalmology. Eye Symptoms.
key_use_and_limit: Sudden vision changes or loss and eye pain can require emergency attention.

citation: ISO 9241-5:2024. Ergonomics of human-system interaction—Part 5: Workstation layout and postural requirements.
key_use_and_limit: Use as a professional reference for layout and adjustability; do not reproduce proprietary standard text.

citation: Apple Developer. Human Interface Guidelines—Accessibility.
key_use_and_limit: Interfaces should remain usable with assistive technologies and accessibility settings.
